trainees.name: Alejandro Gallego-Ortega
trainees.title: Postdoctoral Scholar
trainees.description: My research focuses on understanding how retinal diseases, particularly glaucoma, affect the structure and function of retinal ganglion cells, the neurons responsible for transmitting visual information from the retina to the brain. I am particularly interested in how changes in dendritic architecture relate to alterations in their receptive fields—the regions of the visual field that influence neuronal responses to visual stimuli—and how these structural and functional changes may contribute to visual dysfunction in glaucoma.

trainees.name: Yasmine Tani
trainees.title: Staff Research Associate
trainees.description: Yasmine studies different ways to analyze the responses of retinal ganglion cells to varying stimuli, using multi-electrode array recordings. She is particulary interested in contributing to robust analysis pipelines for comparing electrophysiological experiments at different light levels.

trainees.name: Anushka Narasani
trainees.title: Lab Assistant I
trainees.description: Anushka is researching morphological diversity in retinal ganglion cells that project to the superior colliculus, and computational tools to analyze and classify those cells.

trainees.name: Christopher Meredith
trainees.title: PhD Student
trainees.description: Through the use of microspectrophotometry and ex-vivo electroretinograms, Chris investigates the light-driven visual pigment regeneration that allows cones to remain sensitive to stimuli. While his primary focus is on cones, he has also done work studying the effects of pigment lifetime in rod dark adaptation.

trainees.name: Annabelle Tran
trainees.title: Staff Research Associate I
trainees.description: Annabelle investigates how metabolism shapes rod photoreceptor computation and how retinal circuits remodel during degeneration, using ex-vivo electroretinography and targeted pharmacology.

trainees.name: Huakun Li
trainees.title: Postdoctoral Scholar
trainees.description: Huakun Li is a postdoctoral scholar in the Field Lab. He is passionate about developing state-of-the-art functional interrogation platforms to advance retinal physiology research.

trainees.name: Maya Alexandra Carleton
trainees.title: Postdoctoral Fellow
trainees.description: Maya is a postdoctoral researcher in the Field lab. Her current research interests focus on understanding how the retina allocates energy for encoding visual signals and how it may be perturbed in disease.

trainees.name: Nilou Ghazavi
trainees.title: PhD Candidate
trainees.description: Nilou is interested in understanding how different retinal ganglion cell (RGC) types contribute to downstream visual processing and perception. Her research focuses on developing a computational framework to design visual stimuli that can selectively manipulate the activity of specific RGC types.

trainees.name: Ting-Hao Liu
trainees.title: PhD Candidate
trainees.description: Ting-Hao’s research focuses on sensing and control for medical robotics, image-processing algorithms, and fluidic pump control systems. His current work involves developing multimodal sensing technologies to assist surgeons in performing procedures within the confined orbital region.

trainees.name: Matthew Nepo
trainees.title: PhD Candidate
trainees.description: Matthew studies electromechanical properties of the eye, in the context of their use as diagnostic and surgical planning tools. His research focuses on bioimpedance for tissue diagnostics and simulation of scleral elasticity for intravitreal injection optimization.

trainees.name: Eli Neimark
trainees.title: Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus Fellow
trainees.description: Dr. Eli Neimark conducts research on strabismus, leveraging large-scale datasets and artificial intelligence to investigate its underlying causes and optimize surgical dosing.

trainees.name: Ahmad Santina
trainees.title: Senior Clinical Research Coordinator
trainees.description: Ahmad Santina, MD, is a Senior Clinical Research Coordinator at the Stein Eye Institute. His research focuses on ophthalmic epidemiology, health disparities, and access to eye care, with an emphasis on identifying sociodemographic and clinical factors associated with ocular disease and treatment outcomes. He coordinates,contributes, and leads research projects using electronic health records, large-scale databases, and community-based vision screening data to inform clinical practice and public health policy.

trainees.name: Diana Ibrahim
trainees.title: PhD Student, Molecular Biology IDP
trainees.description: Diana studies the spatial and temporal mechanisms that control the development of the human fovea.

trainees.name: Sakin Kirti
trainees.title: PhD Student, Bioinformatics IDP
trainees.description: With a background in machine learning, Sakin studies how the retina encodes visual information, using information theory and machine learning to ask why the retina has so many distinct ganglion cell types. He is also interested in comparing computer vision models to the retina, with the goal of using insights from biological vision to build better computer vision systems.

trainees.name: Ying Zheng
trainees.title: Data Analyst III
trainees.description: Data Analysis

trainees.name: Nathapon Treewipanon
trainees.title: Visiting Fellow
trainees.description: His research focuses on multimodal imaging in uveitis, with a particular interest in using advanced imaging to better assess and monitor ocular inflammation. He is also involved in studies of long-term outcomes in posterior uveitis.

trainees.name: Saki Sakakura
trainees.title: postdoctoral scholar
trainees.description: My research interest is to investigate into the mechanism of extracellular vesicles treatment to corneal scar.

trainees.name: Saad Idrees
trainees.title: Postdoctoral Scholar
trainees.description: Saad works at the intersection of neuroscience and machine learning, developing interpretable, accurate, and generalizable computational models of retinal circuits under natural viewing conditions. He uses these models to investigate how the retina encodes information, particularly at scales that are difficult to access experimentally. His broader interests include using biologically grounded models to probe mechanisms underlying retinal diseases, and developing bio-inspired AI architectures that enable generalization to unfamiliar conditions.

trainees.name: Maddie Canter
trainees.title: Staff Research Associate III
trainees.description: Maddie is the lab manager of the Cornea Biology Laboratory. She also serves as the GMP team lead for an ongoing Phase I clinical trial for autologous limbal stem cell transplants, and a pre-clinical trial focusing on corneal stromal scar repair using extracellular vesicles.

trainees.name: Yu-Wen Hung
trainees.title: Postdoctoral Scholar
trainees.description: Yu-Wen investigates the mechanisms by which small molecules activate Wnt in limbal stem cells, assesses dose-dependent toxicity, and explores potential translational studies for safe clinical applications in LSC deficiency.

trainees.name: Arushi Somani
trainees.title: Undergraduate
trainees.description: Arushi studies microRNAs involved in corneal stem cell function and regeneration. Her research focuses on identifying miRNA biomarkers associated with corneal stem and progenitor cells.

trainees.name: xiaoqingsong
trainees.title: Postdoctoral Scholar
trainees.description: Multi-Omics Profiling of Corneal Stromal Stem Cell-Derived Extracellular Vesicles Identifies Functional Biomarkers for Corneal Scarring

trainees.name: Kyle Kim
trainees.title: PhD Candidate
trainees.description: My broad interests largely focus on the mechanisms of neurodegenerative diseases. My current dissertation work focuses on how bipolar cells respond to loss of photoreceptor input in retinal degeneration (i.e. retinitis pigmentosa).

trainees.name: Rikard Frederiksen
trainees.title: Assistant Researcher
trainees.description: Rikard studies adaptation mechanisms in photoreceptors and bipolar cells.

trainees.name: Simran Purohit
trainees.title: Undergraduate
trainees.description: Simran studies how vitamin A-derived lipid accumulation leads to inflammation in STGD1 mouse models using Western blots.

trainees.name: Yasamin Sadat Mousavimotlagh, MD
trainees.title: Research Fellow
trainees.description: Yasamin Sadat Mousavi Motlagh, MD, is a Research Fellow at the UCLA Jules Stein Eye Institute, focusing on innovative microsurgical techniques, robotic technologies, and image-guided ophthalmic surgery. Her research includes whole-eye transplantation, with an emphasis on orbital and skull-base surgical anatomy, vascular access, and intraoperative imaging. She also contributes to research on robotic-assisted ophthalmic microsurgery and advanced retinal therapeutic delivery techniques, including subretinal injections. Her work aims to improve surgical precision, safety, and outcomes through interdisciplinary research and technological innovation.

trainees.name: Marija Rudzite
trainees.title: PhD Candidate
trainees.description: I'm a “bi-coastal” graduate student at Duke Neurobiology Ph.D. program working with the Sommer Lab to understand what visual signals the retina sends to different brain regions. I'm also interested in how the synaptic organization of retinal circuits relates to mathematical descriptions of neural code and visual processing. As a training retinal physiologist, I spend most of my time in the dark, but when I do see the light, I love to be outside hiking, gardening, or biking.

trainees.name: Eesha Vaghasia
trainees.title: Undergraduate
trainees.description: Eesha studies how the expression of the ABCA4 gene can influence various inflammasome pathways in relation to photoreceptors and the RPE. Her current research focuses on the activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome and subsequent age related acceleration of Stargardt Disease.

trainees.name: Menglin Li
trainees.title: Postdoctoral Scholar
trainees.description: Menglin studies how primate fovea is developed using spatial transcriptomics and single-cell multiomics

trainees.name: Xiangmei Zhang , MD
trainees.title: Staff Research Associate IV
trainees.description: Our research focuses on retinal development and the differentiation of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and photoreceptors, with the ultimate goal of establishing retinal disease models and developing curative gene therapies. Alongside my research, I serve as the lab manager, overseeing lab administrative and non-scientific operations to ensure daily efficiency. In this role, I manage mouse colonies, train incoming lab members, and simultaneously carry multiple scientific projects to drive our research goals forward.

trainees.name: Varsha Venkataraman
trainees.title: Undergraduate
trainees.description: Varsha studies retinal ganglion cell morphology in primate models, using neuron tracing, confocal microscopy, and histology to characterize and classify cell types.

trainees.name: Nicole Lui
trainees.title: Undergraduate
trainees.description: Nicole reviews and grades Optical Coherence Tomography images from Age-related Macular Degeneration cohorts, documenting differences in structural features and disease severity. She identifies imaging characteristics that may define clinically significant AMD subgroups and evaluates whether these phenotypes are associated with specific genetic variants.

trainees.name: Fazil Onuralp Ardic
trainees.title: PhD Student
trainees.description: Fazil Onuralp develops machine learning models of retinal activity to better understand neural computations underlying vision. His research focuses on modeling retinal ganglion cell responses to dynamic visual stimuli, with an emphasis on temporal processing, neural dynamics, and context-dependent visual encoding.
